title: Effective-resistance average bound for intrinsic kinetic rows
question: Can the intrinsic kinetic graph use an electrical effective-resistance average to produce a tree-independent finite Poincare lower bound and a cleaner target for cutoff and volume uniformity?
method: For each conditional law pi, form the symmetric momentum conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi), its Laplacian L, and the Moore--Penrose inverse on the positive spectrum.
Compute every pair resistance R_xy=(e_x-e_y)^T L^+ (e_x-e_y) and the unordered Gibbs pair average Rbar_pi=sum_{x<y} pi_x*pi_y*R_xy.
Use the pairwise Cauchy--Schwarz identity to test Var_pi(f)<=Rbar_pi E(f) on every actual-likelihood row, then compare Rbar_pi^-1 with the exact intrinsic gap and the R-407 tree bound.
Repeat the complete volume-two cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and collar-orientation grid in primary and independently reconstructed lanes.
Use a diagonal-q disconnected mutation and a three-node unordered-pair factor test to stress the zero mode, normalization and factor of two.
finding: The primary lane passes 43630/43630 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 43630/43630; the hostile lane passes 6/6; the integrated verifier passes 37/37; and Lean R408 compiles. The exact intrinsic gap range is [0.7570174175402339,5.647863075935321], the resistance-average range is [0.44413751605180657,2.0052069566897672], and the tree-independent lower-bound range is [0.49870164107689835,2.251554898783544]. The smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue is 0.020747640155030216, the largest pair resistance is 85.99011817086337, and the minimum residual is roundoff (-1.0641664309263875e-25).
decision_reason: This advances a tree-independent finite interface: a future analytic proof can target a weighted Green-kernel or resistance-average upper bound rather than a selected path family. The finite data do not establish that the resistance average is bounded under cutoff, volume, phase or exhaustion limits, so no analytic gate is closed.

adversarial_review.check: A three-node unit path gives Rbar=4/9 and bound=9/4; doubling the bound leaves residual -1.
The resistance routine requires exactly d-1 eigenvalues above the 1e-14 floor and rejects a disconnected Laplacian.
Replacing p by diagonal q produces zero off-diagonal conductances and zero positive spectrum; the hostile lane catches it.
All probabilities, eigenvalues, pair resistances, averages and residuals are finite and residuals stay above -1e-8 on the fixture.
The second lane rebuilds the finite oscillator, Gibbs, history, conditional graph and resistance data without importing the R-408 primary module and agrees within 5e-6.
Finite resistance positivity does not prove a cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform Green-kernel estimate, a common core, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite effective-resistance checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
next_action: Construct a cutoff- and volume-independent weighted Green-kernel or resistance-average bound on one Hamiltonian common core, control source, phase and exhaustion dependence, then transfer the bound to the R-399 shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual split. Stop or redesign if the resistance average diverges or the positive spectrum collapses.
no_overclaim: The electrical certificate removes tree choice from the finite bound and exposes a Green-kernel uniformity target; it is not an analytic regulator, thermodynamic, physical-sector or QFT estimate.
